name: Probe handler set
purpose: Owns the HTTP handlers each shipped profile binds. Each handler is a pure function of the resolved profile's response contract and the readiness predicate the profile installed. The handler set contains no per-profile branching outside this module; the resolver's profile object selects which handlers get built. The response body is generated strictly from the profile's enumerated response contract, so a field never appears on the wire that the contract did not declare.
responsibilities: Build a liveness HTTP handler that returns the profile's pass response when the event loop is responsive and the profile's fail response otherwise (AC-14101-1, AC-14102-1, AC-14102-2).

Build a readiness HTTP handler that reads the operator-declared readiness predicate on invocation, returns the profile's pass response when the predicate is pass, and returns the profile's fail response when it is fail (AC-14102-3).

Build a single-signal health HTTP handler for profiles whose `semanticModel` equals `singleHealthSignal` (loadBalancer, uptimeMonitor, reverseProxy): the same predicate drives one handler whose pass and fail responses respect the profile's response contract, with content-length zero for body-less profiles (AC-14103-3, AC-14105-1, AC-14106-3).

Build a Kubernetes JSON handler whose parsed body is exactly `{"status":"pass"}` or `{"status":"fail"}` and no other keys, refusing at build time a contract that includes a field beyond `status` (AC-14105-2, AC-14106-2).

Refuse to emit any string on any handler response that matches an operator-declared dependency name, environment name, hostname, replica id, build hash, or commit sha; the response-writer is generated per profile response contract and cannot include a field the contract did not enumerate (AC-14106-1).
internalStructure: One module exporting a `buildHandlerSet({ profile, readinessPredicate, now })` function. The function returns a `{ handlers }` object whose keys match the profile's resolved probe path set (`/live`, `/ready` for kubernetes; `/health` for loadBalancer; the resolved path for others). Each handler is an async function `(req, res)` that reads the current pass or fail answer, chooses the pass or fail branch of the profile's response contract, and writes the response. The response-writer is a per-profile pure function generated from the contract; there is no shared writer that could accidentally include a field the contract omitted.

interfaces.name: buildHandlerSet
interfaces.description: buildHandlerSet({ profile, readinessPredicate, now }) -> { handlers }. `profile` is the frozen object from TAC-1501. `readinessPredicate` is a project-supplied `() -> 'pass' | 'fail'` function (default: strict-any-fail over declared dependency cached state). `now` is a `() -> Date` for test isolation. Returns a map of resolved path to stateless async handler. Called once at boot.

interfaces.name: readinessPredicate
interfaces.description: Project-supplied synchronous function returning the current readiness state as `'pass'` or `'fail'`. The handler set never reads dependency state directly; the predicate boundary is where per-project logic lives.

dependencies.name: profile resolver
dependencies.description: Reads the frozen profile object this component builds handlers against.

tradeoffs: The handler-set builder generates one response-writer per profile response contract; there is no polymorphic writer shared across profiles. This costs a small amount of duplication (the pass and fail branches for each profile shape are separate) and buys the invariant that a handler cannot emit a field the profile contract did not enumerate. The alternative (one generic writer that reads a field list at runtime) leaks the field-list surface into every handler and re-opens the class REQ-006 exists to close.
